new_statements.quote: The answer to that question is that Malieng is clearly an iambic language in word-structure. Morphemes of more than one syllable consist of a presyllable with limited phonological contrasts, followed by a main syllable. Compounds tend to be lexicalised into sesquisyllabic structures likewise. [p. 359] [...] Within this sesquisyllabic structure, the stress is borne in the second element (i.e. the main syllable), which preserves its original tonation category. The first element is lenited both segmenally and suprasegmentally, becoming toneless (indicated with a superscript 0). [p. 353]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Malieng is a tonal ('tonation': 5 tonal categories x 2 phonation registers) language whose words are monosyllables or iambic sesquisyllables; in any polysyllabic word or lexicalised compound the stress falls on the final (main) syllable, which alone carries tone, while the preceding presyllable is unstressed, reduced and toneless.
new_statements.exceptions: Coordinate compounds tend to keep a full disyllabic form (p. 383), and sesquisyllabised compounds are realised as full disyllables in careful/didactic speech; sentence-final particles may change tonal category (intonation). No tone sandhi reported. No exceptions to iambic word prominence are stated.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (and, per the author, also phrase-level 'iambic' structure, e.g. preposition+noun binary phrases reduced to sesquisyllables). Section 5.9.2 is explicitly labelled by the author as 'almost just a placeholder' answering whether disyllables are iambic or trochaic; no instrumental stress study.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement source (Badosa Roldós 2025) describes Malieng / Mã Liềng of Hà Tĩnh and Quảng Bình provinces, Vietnam (author gives ISO 639-3 'pkt or bgl'; ~1,250 speakers, six villages); Glottolog lists Malieng and Mã Liềng as alternative names of male1282 (Maleng), so the match is direct, although Wikipedia notes that Chamberlain 2003 / Sidwell 2009 treated 'Malieng' as a Chut [scb, chut1247] dialect while Babaev & Samarina 2021 group Mã Liềng with Maleng. The secondary source Ferlus 1997 describes Maleng Brô, the Laos variety (Kha Phong / Maleng Kari cluster, Khammouane), also under male1282 per the Wikipedia/Babaev-Samarina dialect list.

sources.note: Ch. 5 (suprasegmentals, pp. 221-359): Malieng is 'clearly an iambic language in word-structure' (5.9.2, p. 359); in sesquisyllables 'the stress is borne in the second element (i.e. the main syllable)', the presyllable is lenited and toneless (5.8.6, p. 353); tonation system of 5 tonal categories x 2 registers; no tone sandhi; repeated in Ch. 6-7 (pp. 379-383).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Maleng language' (raw wikitext), citing Babaev & Samarina 2021: 12 for dialect clusters
sources.note: Nothing on stress; notes Maleng has a Thavung-type four-way register system with pitch (citing Sidwell); groups Mã Liềng, Kha Pakatan, Malang, and the Kha Phong/Maleng Kari/Maleng Bro cluster under Maleng, but also reports Chamberlain 2003 / Sidwell 2009 treating 'Malieng' as a Chut dialect.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1997. Le maleng brô et le vietnamien. Mon-Khmer Studies 27: 55-66 (HAL halshs-01133665, author version).
sources.note: Maleng Brô (Laos variety): words are monosyllables or quasi-disyllables of presyllable + main syllable; 'La présyllabe est une syllabe réduite non-accentuée; elle comporte moins de consonnes que la syllabe normale et n'a pas de voyelle pertinente' (HAL p. 4, section 'La structure syllabique'). No separate stress statement beyond this.
